newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-MEXICO WINS REVENGE OVER UNITED STATES IN U.S. CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO WINS REVENGE OVER UNITED STATES IN U.S. CUP.

text.p: Mexico gained revenge Sunday for a recent string of poor performances against the United States, easily beating the Americans 2-0 in the U.S. Cup soccer tournament.

Goals from veterans Luis Roberto Alves and captain Alberto Garcia Aspe were enough for the visitors to gain their first victory over the Americans in the last six attempts, including a stunning loss to the United States in the 1995 Copa America.

Earlier, in the first game off a double-header at the Rose Bowl, Denmark beat Peru 2-1, on a goal by Danish defender Soren Colding, who rocketed home a right-foot volley from 20 metres in the 81st minute.
Soren Andersen had put the Danes ahead in the eight minute and Peru had equalised through Nolberto Solano Todco early in the second half.
For Mexico, it was their first victory against their old rivals on U.S. soil since a 1-0 win in Dallas in 1974 -- a string of eight matches.

It was a disappointing loss for the Americans who were playing without injured key players including captain John Harkes, his midfield partner Tab Ramos and all-time leading U.S. scorer Eric Wynalda. In addition, stopper Tomas Dooley is playing for his club Schalke in the German Bundesliga.

It was the second loss in the four-nation tournament for the Americans, whose coach Steve Sampson says he is experimenting with several young players before the CONCACAF group World Cup final qualifying round later this year.

Doubly disappointing for the home team was that Mexico is now coached by Bora Milutinovic, who formerly coached the Americans and led them to a surprising second-round berth in the 1994 World Cup. Sampson was his assistant then.

Sunday's match was a warm-up for crucial group play in which the United States, Mexico, Canada, Jamaica, El Salvador and Costa Rica will be vying for three spots in the 1998 World Cup finals in France.

Mexico came out fired up and went ahead after only three minutes when Aspe's through ball beat the offside trap and set Alves free on the left. He drew defender Mike Burns before shooting low past goalkeeper Brad Friedel from a sharp angle.
In the 68th minute, Aspe put the contest beyond doubt when he latched on to a pass from Benjamin Galindo and beat Friedel with a left-foot blast from the edge of the area.

The closest the disjointed Americans came to scoring was a low, angled shot from Cobi Jones that beat goalie Adolfo Rios but shaved the post. In addition, Joe-Max Moore had two fierce free-kicks, one which whistled high and a second that forced Rios to tip over.

Peru, which beat the United States 1-0 in its first U.S. Cup game on Friday, will play Mexico on Wednesday in Pasadena. The Danes, who lost their first match of the tournament to Mexico 3-1, will play the United States the same night.

United States: Brad Friedel, Mike Burns, Alexi Lalas, Jeff Agoos, Jason Kreis (Frankie Hejduk, 59th minute), Martin Vasquez (Preki Radosavljevic, 52nd), Claudio Reyna, Joe-Max Moore, Cobi Jones, Brian McBride (Roy Lassiter, 64th), Jovan Kirovski (Dan Calichman, 70th)

Mexico: Adolfo Rios, Claudio Suarez, Duilio Davino, Ramon Ramirez, Alberto Garcia Aspe (Marcelino Bernal, 75th), Luis Roberto Alves (Luis Hernandez, 56th), Pavel Pardo, Alberto Coyote, Benjamin Galindo, Enrique Alfaro (Nicolas Ramirez, 83rd), Carlos Hermosillo (Luis Garcia, 66th)
